title: Produce a Consolidated Story Analysis Run Report

story.so_that: certification evidence and workflow reliability can be reviewed without reconstructing runs from scattered logs
story.i_want: each terminal workflow run summarized in one structured report and included in an auditable success-rate aggregate

target_persona.name: Story Analysis Workflow Certification Owner
target_persona.role: Certification owner responsible for workflow evidence and reliability metrics

journey.before: Reviews terminal workflow runs, activity logs, ATIF usage exports, and outcome annotations to understand how each run completed.
journey.during: Inspects a consolidated per-run report and an aggregate success-rate metric that includes status counts, formula, sample window, and manual-intervention count.
journey.after: Presents auditable run evidence and reproducible success metrics to certification examiners without reconstructing runs from scattered logs.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Produce one schema-versioned report for each terminal workflow run and aggregate visible reports into auditable success-rate metrics
inputs: Terminal workflow run metadata (workflow_id, run_id, story_document, final_status, attempt_count, terminal outcome origin)
Executed activity attempt records (step name, activity type, attempt, model, permission mode, duration, output path)
cost_usd when supplied by the supported usage source
Collection of visible terminal-run reports for aggregation
Certification-owner decision on sample window, success formula, and threshold
outputs: Success-rate aggregate with status counts, formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count
Explicit unavailable cost representation when cost_usd is absent
state_changes: A terminal run becomes auditable from a single report file
A collection of reports yields a reproducible end-to-end success metric
Cost fields are marked unavailable rather than estimated when absent

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a workflow reaches a terminal state, when completion processing finishes, then exactly one schema-valid report exists for its workflow_id and run_id.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow reaches a terminal state When completion processing finishes Then exactly one schema-valid {workflow}.report.json exists for its workflow_id and run_id
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Obtain one auditable report per workflow run

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a run contains retries, when the report is read, then every activity attempt appears once in execution order and retry attempts are not collapsed or double-counted.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a run contains activity retries When the report is read Then every activity attempt appears once in execution order and retries are not collapsed or double-counted
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Inspect every activity attempt in execution order

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given usage metrics are available in ATIF, when the report is written, then prompt, completion, and cached token totals match the source data and the raw ATIF artifact remains available.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given usage metrics are available in ATIF When the report is written Then prompt, completion, and cached token totals match the source data and the raw ATIF artifact remains available
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Trust token usage totals from the raw ATIF artifact

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given cost_usd is absent from ATIF, when the report is written, then cost is explicitly unavailable and no estimated value is invented.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given cost_usd is absent from ATIF When the report is written Then cost is explicitly unavailable and no estimated value is invented

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the run ends through automated failure, human accept, or human abort, when the report is read, then the final status and outcome origin distinguish those paths.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the run ends through automated failure, human accept, or human abort When the report is read Then the final status and outcome origin distinguish those terminal paths
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Distinguish how each run was resolved

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given report generation is interrupted, when evidence is inspected, then no truncated report is accepted as complete and rerunning completion for the same run produces one valid result.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given report generation is interrupted When evidence is inspected Then no truncated report is accepted as complete and rerunning completion for the same run produces one valid result

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given concurrent workflows and activity retries, when their reports are generated, then records remain isolated by workflow, run, activity, and attempt.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given concurrent workflows and activity retries When their reports are generated Then records remain isolated by workflow, run, activity, and attempt

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a set of visible reports, when aggregation runs, then it publishes status counts, the defined success formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count, with each observation traceable to one report.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a set of visible reports When aggregation runs Then it publishes status counts, the defined success formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count with each observation traceable to one report

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given retries occur within a run, when the success rate is calculated, then the run contributes at most one observation to the denominator.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given retries occur within a run When the success rate is calculated Then the run contributes at most one observation to the denominator
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Count each run once in success-rate denominator

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Automated tests cover passed, repaired, human-accepted, human-aborted, and automated-failure reports, missing usage fields, partial writes, retries, and concurrent runs.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the consolidated report implementation is complete When the automated test suite runs Then it covers passed, repaired, human-accepted, human-aborted, and automated-failure reports, missing usage fields, partial writes, retries, and concurrent runs
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Verify consolidated report behavior with automated tests
